note: Decisions of src/manifest-block.mjs over test/rig/manifest-fixtures.mjs. The reader is a BYTE grammar: one canonical opening tag, exactly one occurrence, content to the first </script. Position in the document is irrelevant by design. This corpus was originally built to attack an HTML-tokenizer implementation against a real headless browser — it is kept because those are the hardest inputs anyone has aimed at this reader, and every row now has an answer reachable by reading the grammar rather than by running a browser.

fixtures.name: F01-baseline-v1-head
fixtures.why: the 9 seeded components' actual shape (head, after </style>)

fixtures.name: F02-baseline-v2-body-minified
fixtures.why: bill-calendar/keep-in-touch shape: block in BODY, one minified line, v2

fixtures.name: F03-duplicate-id
fixtures.why: two blocks with the same id — which one wins? (author error / smuggling)

fixtures.name: F04-inside-template
fixtures.why: template content is an INERT DocumentFragment: getElementById cannot see it. A naive regex CAN. Differential + smuggling surface.

fixtures.name: F05-inside-comment
fixtures.why: commented-out block: not in the DOM at all. A naive regex sees it. Differential.

fixtures.name: F06-literal-close-in-json-string
fixtures.why: a JSON string value containing a LITERAL </script>: the HTML tokenizer ends the element there, so the JSON is truncated. Establishes 'to the first literal close tag' as the browser rule.

fixtures.name: F07-escaped-close-in-json-string
fixtures.why: the CORRECT way to carry the sequence (<\/script>) — must round-trip identically on both sides

fixtures.name: F08-double-escape-state
fixtures.why: HTML script-data-DOUBLE-escaped state: after <!-- ... <script the NEXT </script> does NOT end the element. The classic place where 'first literal close' diverges from the browser.

fixtures.name: F09-case-and-quote-variants
fixtures.why: tag/attr names are ASCII-case-insensitive, attr order free, quotes optional — the regex must not be literal-string matching

fixtures.name: F10-id-value-wrong-case
fixtures.why: the id VALUE is case-sensitive even though the attr NAME is not: id=OMA-MANIFEST must NOT match

fixtures.name: F11-type-wrong-case-and-padded
fixtures.why: type value casing/whitespace: does el.type-based matching accept APPLICATION/JSON or ' application/json '?

fixtures.name: F12-decoy-first-wrong-type
fixtures.why: SECURITY: an EXECUTABLE script carries the id first; a real json block follows. 'getElementById then check type' -> null; 'first element matching BOTH' -> the second block. Real divergence between two plausible grammars.

fixtures.name: F13-gt-inside-quoted-attribute
fixtures.why: a quoted attribute value containing '>' — the tag does NOT end there. Kills the <script[^>]*> regex shape.

fixtures.name: F14-no-block
fixtures.why: the overwhelmingly common case today: no declaration at all (must mean 'keep the column as-is')

fixtures.name: F15-empty-object-block
fixtures.why: EXPLICIT empty declaration = the 'clear the column' signal in the approved 3-state semantics

fixtures.name: F16-whitespace-only-block
fixtures.why: block present but content is whitespace: is this 'clear' or 'malformed'? Semantics gap that must be decided, not discovered.

fixtures.name: F17-bad-json
fixtures.why: trailing comma / comment — malformed JSON must be a LOUD reject, never a silent 'no block' (that would clear or freeze a declaration by accident)

fixtures.name: F18-json-array-not-object
fixtures.why: valid JSON, wrong top-level type — must not reach Object.entries and throw inside the write tx

fixtures.name: F19-v1-legacy-block
fixtures.why: the 9 shipped components are manifest_version:1 — a v2 engine must still extract them (and settings.html:651 currently HARD-rejects anything !== 1, the mirror hazard)

fixtures.name: F20-unterminated-block
fixtures.why: no closing tag at all (truncated authoring / a save cut mid-write): browser takes the rest of the document as script text

fixtures.name: F21-close-tag-with-space-and-attrs
fixtures.why: '</script >' and '</script foo=bar>' also end a script element per the tokenizer; '</scriptx>' does not

fixtures.name: F22-inside-table-foster-parenting
fixtures.why: foster parenting relocates nodes out of <table>: the element still exists in the DOM, but its position moves — a position-based extractor must not care

fixtures.name: F23-noscript-and-textarea-decoys
fixtures.why: raw-text/escapable-raw-text containers: <textarea> content is TEXT (never an element), <noscript> in a scripting-enabled parse is also raw text. A regex sees elements where the DOM has none.

fixtures.name: F24-svg-namespaced-script
fixtures.why: an SVG <script> is a DIFFERENT element (SVGScriptElement, no .type coercion the same way) yet carries the same id — namespace confusion

fixtures.name: F25-html-entities-in-json
fixtures.why: script content is RAW TEXT: " is NOT decoded. A parser that decodes entities (or an html-to-text pass) corrupts the JSON.

fixtures.name: F27-decoy-inside-another-scripts-js-string
fixtures.why: TOP smuggling risk: another module script's JS source contains the manifest block as a STRING. Script content is raw text, so the DOM has no such element — a flat scanner would extract from inside JS.

fixtures.name: F28-decoy-inside-style-and-xmp
fixtures.why: raw-text containers other than script: <style> and <xmp> also swallow markup as text

fixtures.name: F29-duplicate-attribute
fixtures.why: the tokenizer keeps the FIRST occurrence of a duplicated attribute; a naive last-wins regex reads the second

fixtures.name: F30-self-closing-attempt
fixtures.why: '/>' does NOT close an HTML script element — the rest of the document becomes its content

fixtures.name: F31-nested-template
fixtures.why: template content is parsed as NORMAL markup (nesting allowed): a scanner that skips to the first </template> resumes too early and sees a block the DOM never has

fixtures.name: F32-iframe-decoy
fixtures.why: is <iframe> content raw text to the parser? decides whether the scanner must skip it

fixtures.name: F33-block-before-doctype
fixtures.why: markup before the doctype / outside html: the parser relocates it into head — position must not matter

fixtures.name: F26-non-ascii-and-crlf
fixtures.why: dashboard.html really ships curly quotes inside the block; CRLF line endings are a normal authoring accident

fixtures.name: F34-canonical-then-near-miss
fixtures.why: cold-review find: the near-miss check used to run only when NO canonical block existed, so a canonical block plus a differently-spelled attempt was accepted with the second one silently doing nothing — the outcome the check exists to refuse. Order-mirror of F12.
